title: mail-server: prune_email_push for lost accounts; account check only when emailPush changed
description:
Design: docs/design/emailpush.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: E7. Crates: jmap-mail-server, jmap-server (rustdoc only). Size: S.

Spec: draft-ietf-jmap-emailpush-05 §4: on lost account access or capability the server "MUST stop sending" and "MUST remove that account from the emailPush map"; the unknown-account invalidProperties check applies only when the change includes emailPush (jmapio/jmap#478). Design: docs/design/emailpush.md §5.2 (prune), §6, §10 "r44n.3".

Add pub fn prune_email_push(sub: &mut PushSubscription, accounts: &BTreeMap<Id, EmailPushAccount>) -> bool in emailpush/validate.rs: it removes keys not in accounts, keeps {} (not null) when every key goes, and returns whether anything changed. Rustdoc on jmap_server::PushSubscriptionBackend::list_push_subscriptions: EmailPush backends run prune_email_push on what they return (strip on read, the strip_unsupported_chat_push precedent). Rustdoc on EmailPushBackend: the consumer's revocation path calls it and persists. The "only when changed" half is already in check_email_push_change (JMAP-r44n.5); add a unit test pinning it here. Stopping sends is covered by email_pushes_for taking the live account (no entry => []).
Acceptance: unit tests — prune removes only revoked keys, an all-revoked map becomes {} not null, the return value reports change correctly; check_email_push_change on an update whose old and new emailPush are equal passes with a stale account (decision 16: there is no `changed` set; the function compares old and new). The memory end-to-end revocation tests (/get lacks R; an update of types succeeds and the stored map loses R; patch emailPush/R => ["emailPush","emailPush/R"]; patch emailPush/R/urgency => invalidPatch; deliveries to R push nothing) are in the memory backend bead and close this bead's acceptance there.
